title: Only the text decides the blank
statement: In a gap-fill choice, every option should come from the same category, read grammatically in the sentence and differ in meaning there, so only understanding the text decides.
detail: Fill-the-blank choice items came into the evaluator with audits that write each option into the sentence (`shadow-bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/inline_choice_evaluation.txt`). The item fails if any option makes the sentence ungrammatical, since the skill tested is comprehension, not grammar correction, or if two options mean the same thing there, since the blank then has no unique answer. A correct choice must need the passage read and understood; grammar alone, such as article agreement, or common knowledge must not decide it. Then neither grammar nor elimination can decide the blank.

evidence.quote: - Any option produces an ungrammatical sentence when inserted (all options must fit grammatically — the skill being tested is comprehension, not grammar correction).
- Two or more options produce identical meaning in context (the blank has no unique correct answer).
A correct inline choice must require the student to have read and understood the passage — it is NOT acceptable if grammar alone (e.g., article agreement) or common knowledge determines the answer.
